answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The reef multiplier is published, charged in knoll, and summit lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2461 identities would post 3239 proofs and burn roughly 89 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
